name: add_tests_express_endpoint
description: Asks the model to write tests for an already-correct Express endpoint using Node's built-in http module
prompts: The Express server in server.js (already working, do not modify it) listens on port 8026 and exposes GET /square/:n, which returns 200 with JSON {"n": <n>, "square": <n*n>} when :n is a valid integer, or 400 with JSON {"error": ...} when :n is not a valid integer. Write tests in a file named exactly test_server.js. Your test file must: (1) start the server by requiring './server.js' (this has the side effect of calling app.listen), (2) wait briefly for the server to be ready, (3) use only Node's built-in http module (not supertest, not axios - they are not installed) to send at least these requests and assert on the results with Node's built-in assert module: GET /square/4 must return status 200 and body {n:4, square:16}; GET /square/abc must return status 400 with an error field. Print PASS and exit with status 0 if every assertion passes; let an uncaught assertion error (or process.exit(1)) propagate on failure.
